paraphrase.state_paraphrase:
Microwave ovens function by utilizing microwaves to agitate the molecules within food, resulting in uniform heating throughout—both internally and externally—and preventing uneven heating due to external focus. In contrast, induction cookers operate by warming the pot’s base through eddy currents, which then conduct heat from the exterior toward the interior of the food.
